claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs lines 19-22: `await repository.AddAsync(order); await repository.SaveChangesAsync(); notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed"); return order;` — no try/catch anywhere in the method. The lesson's code block (lines 8-23) matches the source character for character.

OrdersController.cs:26-27 @ stage-1: `var order = await orderService.PlaceOrderAsync(customerId, items); return CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order));`. Docs (moniker >= aspnetcore-8.0): "A 201 status code is generated by the CreatedAtAction method when a product is created."

INotifier.cs:7 `void Send(int orderId, string subject);`; ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:16 `services.AddScoped<INotifier, LoggingNotifier>();` (only INotifier registration at stage-1); LoggingNotifier.cs:11-12 body is one `logger.LogInformation(...)` call. Code block lines 9-13 matches the source.

EF Core docs: "By convention, non-composite primary keys of type short, int, long, or Guid are set up to have values generated for inserted entities" and "After SaveChanges completes, all of the entities have been updated with their real key values". Order.Id is int; InitialCreate migration @ stage-1 gives orders.id `NpgsqlValueGenerationStrategy.IdentityByDefaultColumn`.

EF Core docs: "By default, if the database provider supports transactions, all changes in a single call to SaveChanges are applied in a transaction. ... SaveChanges is guaranteed to either completely succeed, or leave the database unmodified". Items are inserted too: "the Add methods ... start tracking an entire graph of related entities, putting them all to the Added state". No outer transaction in OrderService @ stage-1, so the commit precedes Send.

Program.cs:67 `app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>();` is the first Use* call. ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:16-30: catch KeyNotFoundException -> 404, catch ArgumentException -> 400, catch (Exception ex) { logger.LogError(ex, "unhandled exception"); WriteProblemAsync(context, 500, "Server error", "something went wrong"); }.

Docs (moniker >= aspnetcore-6.0): "Each delegate can perform operations before and after the next delegate. Exception-handling delegates should be called early in the pipeline, so they can catch exceptions that occur in later stages of the pipeline." RequestLoggingMiddleware between them @ stage-1 has no try/catch, so it does not stop the exception.

"The await operator suspends evaluation of the enclosing async method until the asynchronous operation represented by its operand completes. ... The await operator doesn't block the thread that evaluates the async method. When the await operator suspends the enclosing async method, the control returns to the caller of the method."

"Threads that belong to the managed thread pool ... are background threads." "Once all foreground threads have been stopped in a managed process ... the system stops all background threads and shuts down." Task objects "perform asynchronous tasks on thread pool threads". No retry: Task.Run takes only the delegate and optional CancellationToken; nothing re-runs a faulted task.

Repo evidence (next stage's real sender): git show stage-2:DonHang.Infrastructure/MailKitEmailSender.cs — `using var client = new SmtpClient { Timeout = 10_000 }; await client.ConnectAsync(smtp.Host, smtp.Port, ...); await client.SendAsync(message, ...);` against mailpit:1025, a separate Compose service reached over the network.

Opinion, and the lesson states it with its condition (the email is not what the customer asked for; the response should not depend on a server the API does not control). No absolute 'always/never' form in the text.
OrderService.cs:34-36 @ stage-1: `order.Status = "cancelled"; await repository.SaveChangesAsync(); notifier.Send(order.Id, "order cancelled");` then `return order;`.

Executed with .NET 10.0.12 (dotnet run of a file-based program printing BaseType chains and IsAssignableFrom): SocketException -> Win32Exception -> ExternalException -> SystemException -> Exception; IOException -> SystemException; TimeoutException -> SystemException; also HttpRequestException -> Exception, OperationCanceledException -> SystemException. All: ArgumentException False, KeyNotFoundException False. ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:16-30 @ stage-1 has only those two specific catches before catch (Exception).

issues.text: The status code is not backed by a line of PlaceOrderAsync: the 500 comes from ExceptionHandlingMiddleware's catch (Exception), as the suggested answer itself says. PlaceOrderAsync only explains why the exception escapes (no try/catch around Send).
